identity.title: Basic Spectroscopic Interpretation
identity.shortDescription: An early draft exploring how absorption and emission spectra are read to reason about molecular structure. Deliberately incomplete and unpublished pending reference and review work.
identity.fullDescription: This record is an intentionally early draft retained to exercise the publication workflow and the unpublished-content restrictions of the platform. Its planned scope is introductory interpretation of simple absorption and emission spectra (colour of solutions, flame emission lines, and the logic of matching spectral features to substances) for undergraduate learners. Scientific sections that have not yet been sourced or reviewed are explicitly marked requires_review rather than filled with plausible-sounding text.

prerequisites: Electronic structure basics and electromagnetic spectrum overview.

learningObjectives: Read simple absorption and emission spectra and relate features to electronic transitions.
Match unknown spectra to reference substances by characteristic features.
State the assumptions and limits of qualitative spectral interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Draft outcome pending educator input: interpret a simple spectrum and justify the assignment of one feature to a transition.

theory.overview: Draft overview: atoms and molecules absorb or emit light at characteristic wavelengths determined by their energy-level structure, so spectra serve as fingerprints for identification and as evidence about structure. This overview is a placeholder summary of the intended scope and must not be treated as reviewed content.
